A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARC research, with matching authors, algorithms and retained experiments. All pages, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–D. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split Imagenet-R, including ARC comparisons, component ablations and empirical validation of its assumptions.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark results, representation analyses, TTA comparisons, threshold sensitivity, timing measurements and final-task-only adaptation results.

M1.justification: The OTD selection rules, frozen-backbone classifier update using cross-entropy plus entropy minimization, and TSS correction remain unchanged. Adding 'Self-' to component names and correcting Algorithm 1's threshold variable clarify the existing procedure. ARC-Last evaluates a different application schedule for the same algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on 5-dataset, combining CIFAR-10, MNIST, FashionMNIST, SVHN and notMNIST (Section 4.1 and Table 2). This substantially broadens the represented image distributions beyond the retained Split CIFAR-100 and Split Imagenet-R benchmarks.

E2.justification: v1 compares continual-learning methods with and without ARC. v2 additionally evaluates TENT with iCarL, Der, Memo and L2P (Table 3), and CoTTA with L2P, DualPrompt, iCarL and Memo (Appendix B). These introduce direct alternative adaptation methods; CoTTA was only discussed in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds 20-task splits through CIFAR-100 Inc5 and Imagenet-R Inc10, while retaining the original 10-task settings. Section 3.2 introduces sequential fine-tuning followed by past-task linear probing across three ViT and three ResNet configurations. Appendix D adds final-task-only ARC evaluation. The main backbone, memory budgets and accuracy/forgetting definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds representation-retention analysis across architectures (Figure 3), sensitivity to beta and gamma (Figure 5), inference overhead measurements (Appendix C), and an adaptation-schedule ablation (Appendix D). It removes v1 Figure 3's per-task accuracy analysis, which exposed current-task degradation. Existing component ablations and assumption-validation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experiments. v2 continues reporting point estimates; additional result rows and threshold curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, comparator and diagnostic results and removes the original per-task results. For the retained Imagenet-R Inc20 setting, L2P+ARC accuracy changes from 74.8 to 75.1, while Der's reported forgetting reduction is corrected from 7.4 to 8.3 points. Figure 1 also has revised curves. New reporting contains inconsistencies: Table 2 labels Memo's 91.9-to-93.0 change as +2.1, and Table 9's ARC values conflict with Table 1.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–2, the training losses, TSS definition and evaluation formulas retain their mathematical content. Renaming the TSS maximization index and metric symbols does not introduce new mathematics. The added representation and time-complexity sections provide empirical evidence rather than proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: v2 adds a substantive introductory claim that pretrained representations lose little information even after unrestricted fine-tuning on later tasks, supported by Section 3.2. v1 merely chose to address classifier bias and illustrated it with a frozen backbone. This extends the contribution to identifying the primary source of forgetting, while retaining ARC's central compatibility and performance claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for ARC's advantage over TENT, greater benefits on longer sequences, and the inference-cost tradeoff. It removes v1's stability–plasticity interpretation of current-task accuracy losses and the concluding limitation concerning dependence on test-sample distribution. These substantially change the account of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies SGD for non-prompt methods, Adam for prompt methods, and batch-level single-update adaptation. v2 also identifies the class-order source and reports relative inference overhead. These expand documentation without establishing changes to existing settings. Hyperparameters are deferred to an unspecified codebase without concrete values or an access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds the TENT reference and removes Boudiaf et al.'s parameter-free online adaptation reference. It adds specific positioning against SLCA's restricted learning rates and explains distinctions from generic TTA. Most continual-learning, OOD and TTA references and the broader research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 renames the title and components to Adaptive Self-Retention/Correction, shortens the TTA overview, and locally rewrites the introduction and experimental narrative. It adds a motivation subsection and appendices, but preserves most existing prose and the main section order.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands to four experimental settings, and six additional tables present new comparisons and analyses; original Tables 2–3 survive as Tables 4–5. The original per-task Figure 3 is removed, while new representation and sensitivity figures are added. Figure 1 is redrawn with a corrected legend, Figure 2's task labels change, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: Broader benchmarks, direct TTA comparisons and sensitivity/timing analyses strengthen the evidence for ARC. However, v2 removes evidence of current-task degradation and the test-distribution limitation, while introducing reporting problems: Table 2 miscalculates Memo's gain, and Table 9 reports L2P+ARC as 64.7 versus Table 1's 75.1 under the same named setting without explanation. The gains in evidential breadth coexist with reduced transparency and inconsistent results, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
